display_title: [jax-buildcop] Seed RNG and pass SVD tolerances to _CompileAndCheck in SvdTest

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Seed RNG and pass SVD tolerances to _CompileAndCheck in SvdTest

testSvdWithRectangularInput and testSingularValues in svd_test.py drew inputs from the unseeded global np.random.uniform, which is non-deterministic across concurrent test threads, and called self._CompileAndCheck without tolerances, defaulting to rtol=1e-15, atol=1e-15 under x64 on singular vectors of ill-conditioned matrices with condition numbers up to 1e9 computed under float32 matmul precision.

Use self.rng().uniform for deterministic per-test seeding and pass rtol=_SVD_RTOL, atol=1E-6 to self._CompileAndCheck to match the singular value assertions in the same tests.

display_title: [JAX] Add F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X{3,4} DotAlgorithmPreset values

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Add F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X{3,4} DotAlgorithmPreset values

Add `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` and `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` to `jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset` and `jax_default_matmul_precision` to expose the StableHLO 1.21.0 3 operation and 4 operation `float8_e4m3fn` dot emulation algorithms for `bfloat16` and `float32` inputs, requiring `jaxlib_extension_version >= 514`.

Unlike `BF16_BF16_F32_X3` (where `bfloat16` and `float32` share an 8 bit exponent), `float8_e4m3fn` has a narrower 4 bit exponent, so operands are scaled into the `float8_e4m3fn` range before decomposing each input into an initial `float8_e4m3fn` term and a scaled `float8_e4m3fn` rounding residual. `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` sums all 4 pairwise `float8_e4m3fn` dot products in `float32` and rescales the result, while `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` drops the residual by residual product for higher throughput.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Use the transposed preconditioner in gmres and bicgstab transpose solves

head_commit.message:
Use the transposed preconditioner in gmres and bicgstab transpose solves

gmres and bicgstab passed the same solve function as both `solve` and
`transpose_solve` to `lax.custom_linear_solve`, so the transpose solve
preconditioned A^T with M. For a nonsymmetric M that approximates A^-1,
M is a poor preconditioner for A^T, and reverse-mode derivatives converge
slowly or not at all even when the forward solve converges.

The transpose solve now uses M^T, computed with `jax.linear_transpose`.
M must therefore be a linear operator, and a function or matmul-compatible
M must be transposable with `jax.linear_transpose`. cg keeps its existing
behavior.

gmres also computed its tolerances from the primal b and reused them in
the transpose solve. When the cotangent is much smaller than b, the
transpose solve returned x0 without iterating. Each solve now computes
its tolerances from the right-hand side it receives, with ptol = 0 for a
zero right-hand side. The forward solve is unchanged.

`b` and `x0` are now passed to separate `device_put` calls. A joint call
made x0 depend on b under `jax.linear_transpose`, which prevented
transposing a preconditioner built from a nested cg or gmres solve.

Fixes #29449

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [AutoPGLE] Sync devices after profiler startup.

head_commit.message:
[AutoPGLE] Sync devices after profiler startup.

This improves measurement quality by removing host-side variability in
when the executable is actually launched under the profiler from the
measured cost of (typically) the first collective in the executable.

Costs are prefixed by the executable fingerprint, so the cost of the
barrier kernel will not pollute the measured costs for the executable of
interest even though it will be captured by the profiler.

Make sure that executables compiled with the same device mesh shape but
different concrete device lists get different PGLE profilers, which is
important now that the PGLE profiler owns a barrier prepared for the
specific set of devices.

display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Validate and lower TMA async copies in transformed space.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Validate and lower TMA async copies in transformed space.

Previously, `_prepare_tma` and `_check_tma_strides_and_swizzle` validated GMEM strides and element bitwidths against the untransformed GMEM reference (`gmem_ref_ty`). This prevented upcoming sub-byte packing transforms from reinterpreting GMEM and SMEM references into packed byte-typed memrefs.

Propagate `gmem_strides` through all transforms in `_prepare_tma` (adding `transform_strides` to `DropUnitDimsTransform` and `CollapseLeadingIndicesTransform`) and validate strides, element bitwidths, and clamping bounds in the transformed space. Also rename `gmem_ref` to `untransformed_gmem_ref` to clearly distinguish pre-transform and transformed references.

display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Support non-power-of-two vector bitwidths in `getelement…

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support non-power-of-two vector bitwidths in `getelementptr` and loads/stores.

When `llvm.getelementptr`, `llvm.load`, or `llvm.store` operates on a vector type whose total bitwidth is not a power of two (such as `vector<12 x
  i4>`, which is 6 bytes), LLVM's `DataLayout` pads the vector's allocation and ABI alignment to the next power of two (8 bytes). This caused
  `getelementptr` to advance pointers by 8 bytes instead of 6 bytes (triggering `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` on out-of-bounds global accesses) and `llvm.
  load`/`llvm.store` without explicit alignment to emit 4-byte-aligned PTX instructions (`ld.shared.u32`/`st.shared.u32`) at 2-byte-aligned offsets
  (`CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS`).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008753068

Update `lt_to_p`, `le_to_p`, and `eq_to_p` to lower floating-point comparisons
to `stablehlo.compare` with `comparison_type = WEAKORDER` when not in
forward-compatibility mode and `jaxlib` (>= 514) and `libtpu` (>= 0.0.52)
support it, and remove explicit zero/NaN canonicalization from
`_operands_to_keys`.

When lowering for forward-compatible export or older `jaxlib`/`libtpu`
versions, fall back to canonicalizing zeros and NaNs via
`_canonicalize_float_for_sort` and emitting `TOTALORDER`.

display_title: Fix precision of jax.scipy.special.ndtr in the negative tail.

head_commit.message:
Fix precision of jax.scipy.special.ndtr in the negative tail.

Previously, `ndtr` in `jax._src.lax.special` computed the negative tail (`x <= -1`) as `0.5 * lax.erfc(|x| / sqrt(2))`, which had up to 252.5-319.0 ULP error in `float32` and 1021.0 ULP error in `float64`:
1. Default-accuracy `lax.erfc` itself has up to 66-157 ULP error in `float32` and 350 ULP error in `float64`.
2. Even calling `0.5 * erfc_impl(-x / sqrt(2))` (`accuracy=AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`) would lose hundreds of ULPs for large negative `x`: `erfc_impl(u)` evaluates a factor of `exp(-u^2)`, and rounding `u = -x / sqrt(2)` to a single float before squaring introduces `~x^2` ULPs of error in `exp(-u^2)`.

Move `ndtr` to `jax._src.lax.erf`, inlining `0.5 * erfc_impl(-x / sqrt(2))` so `exp(-0.5 * x^2)` is evaluated by splitting `x^2 = s_hi + s_lo` into an exact sum of two floats via `_split_square(|x|)` and multiplying both parts by `-0.5`. Also add `@jit` and a custom JVP using `exp_neg_half_sq(x)`.

display_title: [nn] Mask tangents and cotangents with where in _softmax_jvp

head_commit.message:
[nn] Mask tangents and cotangents with where in _softmax_jvp

When `where` is provided to `jax.nn.softmax` with `softmax_custom_jvp=True`:
- Mask the input tangent `x_dot` with `jnp.where(where, x_dot, 0)` so `NaN`/`inf` tangents at masked-out positions do not evaluate `0.0 * NaN = NaN` in forward-mode AD (`jvp`).
- Mask the output tangent `y_dot` with `jnp.where(where, y_dot, 0)` so in reverse-mode AD (`vjp`), incoming `NaN`/`inf` cotangents at masked-out positions (such as from masked entropy/KL terms `jnp.sum(p * jnp.log(p), where=mask)` where `p == 0` at `~mask` produces `0 * (-inf) = NaN`) are zeroed out before multiplying by `y = 0.0` and summing across the reduction axis, matching `_softmax_deprecated` and `jax.nn.log_softmax`.
- Add `NNFunctionsTest.testSoftmaxWhereGradMaskedNan` in `tests/nn_test.py` to test masked `p * log(p)` gradients and masked `NaN` tangents under both `jax.softmax_custom_jvp(False)` and `jax.softmax_custom_jvp(True)`.

display_title: [Pallas:TPU] Expose DMA priority in pipeline helpers and fast slot indexing.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Expose DMA priority in pipeline helpers and fast slot indexing.

Pallas TPU async copy descriptors (`AsyncCopyDescriptor`) and pipeline helpers (`BufferedRef` and `emit_pipeline`) previously lacked persistent controls for DMA queue priority. In pipelined kernels that mix latency-critical input prefetches with background state writebacks or cross-device transfers, issuing all copies on the default queue causes head-of-line DMA blocking. In addition, `BufferedRef` computed ring-buffer slot indices with `lax.rem` on every step, emitting scalar integer remainder instructions in the inner pipeline loop even for power-of-two buffer counts.

Thread `priority` through `AsyncCopyDescriptor`, `make_async_copy`, `make_async_remote_copy`, `BufferedRef`, and `emit_pipeline` so pipelines and custom descriptors can prioritize critical-path prefetches. Replace `lax.rem` in `BufferedRef` slot indexing with bitwise AND when `buffer_count` is a power of two.

display_title: Implement `jax.scipy.special.jn` for static integer orders and real/complex arguments

head_commit.message:
Implement `jax.scipy.special.jn` for static integer orders and real/complex arguments

Implementation details:
- Reduces negative integer orders via `J_{-n}(z) = (-1)^n J_n(z)` and maps real/complex `z` to the first quadrant `w = |Re(z)| + i|Im(z)|`.
- For `n <= 1`, evaluates via ascending power series (`|w| <= 2`), Miller's backward recurrence (`2 < |w| < rl`), and Hankel's asymptotic expansion (`|w| >= rl`).
- For `n >= 2`, uses exact power-of-2 prefactor scaling in the ascending power series (`|w| <= max(2, sqrt(2*(n+1)))`), Miller's backward recurrence for intermediate `|w| < rl`, direct Hankel asymptotic expansion for `|w| >= rl + 0.5*n^2`, and `(J_0, J_1)` + recurrence (with backward continued-fraction ratios across the turning point or away from the real axis) for `rl <= |w| < rl + 0.5*n^2`.
- Adds envelope precision, complex-argument, and gradient tests in `tests/lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`.

display_title: Fix precision of jax.scipy.special.ndtr in the negative tail.

head_commit.message:
Fix precision of jax.scipy.special.ndtr in the negative tail.

Previously, `ndtr` in `jax._src.lax.special` computed the negative tail (`x <= -1`) as `0.5 * lax.erfc(|x| / sqrt(2))`, which had up to 252.5-319.0 ULP error in `float32` and 1021.0 ULP error in `float64`:
1. Default-accuracy `lax.erfc` itself has up to 66-157 ULP error in `float32` and 350 ULP error in `float64`.
2. Even calling `0.5 * erfc_impl(-x / sqrt(2))` (`accuracy=AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`) would lose hundreds of ULPs for large negative `x`: `erfc_impl(u)` evaluates a factor of `exp(-u^2)`, and rounding `u = -x / sqrt(2)` to a single float before squaring introduces `~x^2` ULPs of error in `exp(-u^2)`.

Move `ndtr` to `jax._src.lax.erf`, inlining `0.5 * erfc_impl(-x / sqrt(2))` so `exp(-0.5 * x^2)` is evaluated by splitting `x^2 = s_hi + s_lo` into an exact sum of two floats via `_split_square(|x|)` and multiplying both parts by `-0.5`. Also add `@jit` and a custom JVP using `exp_neg_half_sq(x)`.

head_commit.message:
[pallas:fuser] Check pulled kernel-output block specs in push_pull_block_spec

push_pull_block_spec pushes *block_specs through the output fusion and pulls
the result back via pull_block_spec, but it discarded the pulled specs for the
kernel outputs (*args, **kwargs). When pull(push(bs)) differs from bs, the
returned kernel_fn silently computes the fusion on the wrong blocks. Examples
are reduce_sum or broadcast_in_dim on a squeezed (None) size-1 axis, where
pull rebuilds Blocked(1), and dynamic_update_slice with a pushed operand and a
closed-over update, where pull gives the operand no_block_spec.

For each kernel output the fusion depends on, check that the pulled spec has
the same block shape, memory space and pipeline mode as the pushed one, and
raise a ValueError naming the output otherwise. Kernel outputs the fusion does
not depend on (unused, or only used for their shape) are not checked. Index
maps are not compared, since pulled ones are new compositions through the
fusion.

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules). Bump `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 82 so that Mosaic GPU picks the matching rule types.

Keep `SerdeRuleType` and a `RunSerde` overload that takes `SerdeRuleType` downgrade rules as deprecated aliases, so that JAX versions that predate this change still build.

display_title: Fix hyp1f1 values and gradients for negative x

head_commit.message:
Fix hyp1f1 accuracy near |x| = 100, for terminating series, and in float32

- Truncate the divergent asymptotic series at their smallest term instead
  of summing growing terms up to k = 250.
- Use the terminating series for any x when a is a non-positive integer,
  also for x < 0, where Kummer's transformation does not hold if b is a
  negative integer, and for d/db when x >= 100.
- Stop the series derivatives at vanishing terms, which gave NaN for
  x = 0 and for terminating series with a negative integer b.
- Combine the gamma, exp and power factors of the asymptotic expansions
  in log space, so that they do not overflow separately in float32.
- Differentiate the expansions for x < 0 directly with respect to a and
  b, and compute digamma(b) - digamma(b - a) from its Taylor series for
  small a, to avoid cancellation in d/db.

Lower scan_p with unreduced scanned arrays via HiJAX.

Unreduced constants and carries in `scan_p` already lower via `_scan_to_lojax`,
but for extensive (scanned) `unreduced` inputs and outputs, `ShapedArray.lo_ty`
prepends the `k` per-mesh-axis `unreduced` dimensions ahead of the scanned
sequence dimension (`f32[L, ...]{U:x} --lojax--> f32[2@x, L, ...]`), whereas
LoJAX `scan_p` slices and stacks extensive arrays along dimension 0.

Transpose the scanned sequence dimension to axis 0 before `scan_p.bind` and
back behind the `k` leading `unreduced` dimensions before raising extensive
outputs in `_scan_to_lojax`.

display_title: Lower scan_p with unreduced scanned arrays via HiJAX.

head_commit.message:
Lower scan_p with unreduced scanned arrays via HiJAX.

Unreduced constants and carries in `scan_p` already lower via `_scan_to_lojax`,
but for extensive (scanned) `unreduced` inputs and outputs, `ShapedArray.lo_ty`
prepends the `k` per-mesh-axis `unreduced` dimensions ahead of the scanned
sequence dimension (`f32[L, ...]{U:x} --lojax--> f32[2@x, L, ...]`), whereas
LoJAX `scan_p` slices and stacks extensive arrays along dimension 0.

Transpose the scanned sequence dimension to axis 0 before `scan_p.bind` and
back behind the `k` leading `unreduced` dimensions before raising extensive
outputs in `_scan_to_lojax`.

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules). Bump `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 82 so that Mosaic GPU picks the matching rule types.

Keep `SerdeRuleType` and a `RunSerde` overload that takes `SerdeRuleType` downgrade rules as deprecated aliases, so that JAX versions that predate this change still build.

display_title: Lower unreduced reduce_sum, reduce_max, reduce_min, and copy via HiJAX.

head_commit.message:
Lower unreduced reduce_sum, reduce_max, reduce_min, and copy via HiJAX.

Reduction primitives (`reduce_sum_p`, `reduce_max_p`, `reduce_min_p`) can consume `unreduced` operands, reduce across dropped `unreduced` axes, and introduce new `unreduced` output axes when reducing sharded dimensions without cross-device collectives.

Lower `reduce_sum_p`, `reduce_max_p`, and `reduce_min_p` via `shard_map` manual over the output `unreduced` axes: preserved input `unreduced` axes stay in place as leading singleton dimensions, dropped input `unreduced` axes remain explicit so the inner reduction emits their collectives alongside the logical reduction axes, and newly introduced `unreduced` axes expand into leading singleton dimensions.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Seed RNG and pass SVD tolerances to _CompileAndCheck i…

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Seed RNG and pass SVD tolerances to _CompileAndCheck in SvdTest

testSvdWithRectangularInput and testSingularValues in svd_test.py drew inputs from the unseeded global np.random.uniform, which is non-deterministic across concurrent test threads, and called self._CompileAndCheck without tolerances, defaulting to rtol=1e-15, atol=1e-15 under x64 on singular vectors of ill-conditioned matrices with condition numbers up to 1e9 computed under float32 matmul precision.

Use self.rng().uniform for deterministic per-test seeding and pass rtol=_SVD_RTOL, atol=1E-6 to self._CompileAndCheck to match the singular value assertions in the same tests.

Use `zizmorcore/zizmor-action` over `uvx`.
